decisions.reason: The reference electrometer sits at the core of the firm's decades of dosimetry knowledge, appears on the home page in both years, and is easy for the firm to interpret and improve.

The oncology risk management software builds on the firm's QA software and integration capabilities and has kept its own page for two years, in line with its strategy of merging machine and patient QA.
The CT phantom builds on the firm's imaging QA and phantom expertise, so its in-house R&D can assimilate market feedback and refine it.

Mammography is farther from the firm's radiotherapy core, but its strong R&D, EU research projects and imaging QA activities give it enough related knowledge to learn from early results, though it may be consolidated.
This second, distant mammography phantom overlaps with Product D and carries some risk of being merged away, but the firm's research base and expansion favor keeping it for now.
The broad imaging QA instrument line extends the firm's established measurement expertise and fits its expansion strategy.
